children: , the processor-architecture and silicon company, extended its Muse-fueled run as Wall Street focused on the massive CPU footprint needed to keep agentic AI running. The American depositary shares gained approximately 1.5% to $327.74, keeping the momentum alive as investors looked beyond GPUs to the processors coordinating increasingly complex AI workloads.

The math behind that excitement is big. Arm estimates agentic AI could push data-center CPU demand from roughly 30 million cores to around 120 million cores for every gigawatt of capacity. Management sees a market opportunity topping $100 billion by 2030, while Arm is also pushing beyond its traditional architecture-licensing model through its own AGI CPU platform. That matters because the AI infrastructure story is widening: inference still needs accelerators, but autonomous agents also need enormous amounts of general-purpose compute to organize, route and execute their work.

The valuation now leaves almost no room for a sleepy outcome. At $327.74, Arm trades 68.92% above its GF Value estimate of $194.02, showing just how aggressively the market is pricing future growth into the shares. A fourfold jump in required CPU cores will not automatically produce fourfold royalty revenue; Arm still needs architecture share, favorable chip mix, partner economics and its direct-silicon strategy to convert the workload boom into earnings. Muse makes the demand argument more compelling, but from this valuation, actual server shipments and monetization need to do the heavy lifting.

title: Arm Gains 1.5% as Agentic AI Multiplies CPU Cores
